title: Q14. Character modification through a pointer — Medium-Hard
question: Predict the output.
code:
char s[] = "COMPUTER"; char *p = s;
printf("%c ", *p++); printf("%c ", (*p)++); printf("%c ", *p); printf("%s", s);
explanation: p++ prints C and moves to O; (*p)++ prints O and changes it to P; the final string is CPMPUTER.

title: Q16. String pointers and independent arrays — Advanced
question: Predict the output.
code:

*p = 'Y'; *q = 'Z'; printf("%s ", s); p++; q++; printf("%c %c %s", *p, *q, p);
explanation: The pointers modify the shared array to YEZLO; after both advance, p points to E and q points to L.

title: Q17. Pointer reassignment inside a function — Hard
question: Predict the output.
code:
void fun(int *p) { int x = 100; p = &x; *p = 200; }
int a = 10; int *p = &a; fun(p); printf("%d %d", a, *p);
explanation: The function receives a copy of p. Reassigning that copy does not change the caller's pointer or a.

title: Q18. Double pointer as a function parameter — Hard
question: Predict the output.
code:

int x = 5; int *p = &x; fun(&p); printf("%d %d", x, p == NULL);
explanation: **p changes x, while *p changes the original pointer p in main to NULL.

title: Q20. Recursive calls and return values — Medium-Hard
question: Predict the output.
code:
int fun(int n) { if (n <= 1) return n; return fun(n - 1) + fun(n - 2); }
printf("%d", fun(5));
explanation: This is the Fibonacci recurrence with fun(0)=0 and fun(1)=1.

title: Q21. Recursion with printing before and after the call — Hard
